candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication treatment of opioid use disorder during pregnancy
candidate.educational_objective: Explain why methadone or buprenorphine maintenance is generally preferred to withdrawal for opioid use disorder during pregnancy.

options.A: Opioid agonist pharmacotherapy is recommended in pregnancy and is generally preferred because withdrawal is associated with high relapse rates and worse outcomes
options.B: Methadone eliminates all maternal and neonatal risks from opioid use disorder
options.C: Medically supervised withdrawal is routinely preferred because relapse is uncommon after withdrawal
options.D: Methadone is used only for pain and is not an accepted treatment for opioid use disorder during pregnancy

candidate.rationale: ACOG states that for pregnant patients with opioid use disorder, opioid agonist pharmacotherapy is recommended and is preferable to medically supervised withdrawal because withdrawal is associated with high relapse rates and worse outcomes. Methadone and buprenorphine are established treatments during pregnancy. Maintenance treatment does not eliminate all risk, so B is an unsupported absolute.
candidate.source_claim_supported: In pregnancy with OUD, opioid agonist pharmacotherapy is recommended and generally preferred to medically supervised withdrawal because of relapse and outcome concerns.

candidate.stem: A pregnant client with opioid use disorder asks why methadone maintenance may be continued rather than attempting medically supervised opioid withdrawal. Which explanation is most accurate?
